faqs.q: What is the difference between 3-tab and architectural shingles?

runs.v: Architectural is multi-layer and dimensional, rated up to 130 mph with the 6-nail pattern; 3-tab is one flat layer rated near 60 mph, per ARMA and manufacturer guidance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for asphalt shingle roofing in Orange, NJ?

runs.v: A shingle reroof of a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, with no construction permit; on other buildings, the code's 25% rule applies: repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months needs one. As a rule of thumb, damage over about 25% also favors replacement. Codes matter across Essex County; confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office.

faqs.q: Does an asphalt roof in an Orange historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can; confirm the property's local historic status with the City of Orange Township first. Register listing alone does not restrict a private reroof.

faqs.q: How long do asphalt shingles last in the Orange climate?

runs.v: Around two to three decades: about 30 years for architectural and 20 for 3-tab, varying up to 40% with climate, install, and ventilation, per InterNACHI and the NRCA.

faqs.q: How do you prevent black algae streaks on a new Orange roof?

runs.v: Use algae-resistant shingle lines on shaded slopes, at modest added cost.

faqs.q: How much does asphalt shingle roofing cost in Orange, NJ?

runs.v: A new roof in New Jersey typically costs $10,000–$25,000, the average replacement range per HomeAdvisor and Modernize. A 1,200-square-foot roof is smaller than average, so it usually prices toward the low end; architectural shingles, tear-off, deck repair, and tight-lot access add cost.

faqs.q: How can you tell if a roofer is lying?

runs.v: Reputable New Jersey roofing contractors show Home Improvement Contractor registration (the state's version of licensing), insurance, and a written contract, required for jobs over $500, with three business days to cancel. Red flags: no damage photos, a full-replacement pitch where minor repairs would do, a large cash deposit. A certified contractor allows enhanced manufacturer warranties; compare quality workmanship, durable materials, and long-lasting protection.
